replies.author: AdSoggy8958
replies.body: I've found that supplying chatgpt with ample information/samples, and then asking it to write a prompt, on high level thinking, it gives much better results than if I were to start from scratch and then make change after change after change until I get what I want. Of course that removes a lot of personal flavor, but gives a good base to work from

replies.author: Cpt_Tripps
replies.body:
[Fist Prompt]

First person gameplay in the style of "POV cat cam"

Create a simple scrumban plan for making a cats vs dog chase game. 

Game should include dogs that chase, a playable cat, and a simple hud that shows when a cat is under a car or out in the open.

This is a MVP project to test the gameplay loop.

[Second Prompt]

Using (Game engine and Version info) Follow this scrumban plan to create a MVP.

Error handling and decision making preferences.

comments.author: SentientDreamer

replies.author: AdSoggy8958
replies.body: I updated the OP, I have been doing a lot of work on chatgpt and found that asking it to write a prompt for itself, it tends to include a massive amount of detail that I would have never even thought to include. I examine the prompt before executing it to ensure it's what I'm looking for, then just run the prompt. This was made easy here because I just wanted it to look exactly like the video itself, so I uploaded a screen recording of the video to chatgpt, asked it to make a prompt that would create a game exactly like this video, the result was pretty much exactly this but with a crude dog model, so I did the same for the dog modeling with a full model downloaded from [itch.io](http://itch.io), and this is where it's currently at, I'm going to continue adding better models and textures with this method until it looks how I want it to, and then build the gameloop from that until it's something I find is fun and challenging

replies.author: SentientDreamer
replies.body:
So you went to chatgpt and made it write a prompt for you that would cover what it needs...

Beats my methods, I'm talking to Claude like a colleague and the prototype's being worked on piece by piece.

replies.author: AdSoggy8958
replies.body: You can still use your method, but changing your final step before any changes by asking it to write a prompt, it will fill whatever gaps that may be helpful with keeping your original idea and translating that into something that it digests better.

comments.author: novokvest
comments.body:
Wow, looks great! So much fun. Here are a few unrelated thoughts:

1. True story. When I was little in the 90s we used to go camping to a lake, which was about 200-300 kilometers away from our city. So our friends brought their cat with them. If I remember correctly his name was Samsung but I might be mixing memories. So it was a really badass cat, as it would go hunting, catching wild mice there and then bringing them back to our camp. And when it was time to leave he was nowhere around so his owners had to leave without him. So what do you think? Yup, it came back home - scrawny and battered, but alive! That part really happened - that is an idea for overall theme - eather cat was left accedentally somewhere, or his owners moved or something like that, there are many stories of pet adventures.
2. A more fun take on it which is already in your video is a cat-trouble maker which would steal pies, cakes, milk from neighbourhood and local restaurants occasionally dealing with dogs and people running at him with brooms etc. There would be progressively harder missions involving solving simple puzzles, distracting guards etc.
3. I remember playing a game in the oughts - alien vs predator. What was cool about it - is that predator had his thermal vision, but alien had night vision and could climb surfaces - which is exactly what a cat can do - you MUST implement night vision, climbing curtains etc. Oh and there are trees in your video - cats climb those easily as well!

replies.author: slickriptide
replies.body:
LOL fair point, but it's also true that if you make something that's so similar to another thing that is already popular, that you're going to be compared to it.

Maybe on the original cat cam the legs really do look like they are puppet legs on a stick being waved under the camera. I dunno. But I know that if you wanted to turn this into a game people would download, and maybe even pay a few bucks for it, that it needs to at least look like some devotion went into the graphics.

The beautiful thing about Stray is not the story, not really. It's a fine story. But the joy of it is navigating a cat who looks and acts like a cat. The proof of it is that the dog in the video feels threatening because it looks and moves like a dog. The SVG-animated cat chin and legs, well, it's clear that they represent a cat; but they don't FEEL like a cat. 

I'm not saying the game idea is a bad idea. It needs work like any prototype idea but the initial basic idea could be fun. But it needs more work than just "Make a game out of my cat's cam; don't make mistakes".

comments.author: Cosmic_Jane
comments.body:
I think a fun gameplay loop is kinda like Hitman. But instead of killing people. Maybe you’re tasked with picking up a random object (like a cat toy), and then bringing it to a specific location. 

Start in location A, find an object randomly on the map. Bring it to location B. 

Meanwhile dodging obstacles like dogs or people. And avoiding dangers like water or traps. 

—-

Bonus points if you can kite dogs into traps or find a path that lets you get the toy and return it undetected. 

Hitman is one of my favorite games because I love the sandbox nature of the levels. And the randomness of the objectives. 

I also like how Hitman is a very modern/realistic game setting. Real world like locations. Not space or fantasy. 

So a cat game could include fun levels like outside. But also in a kennel or a supermarket or any other random place a cat can go.
